title: ssh: add decryption for chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com
description:
Decrypt SSH sessions using the chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com cipher
Note: This cipher follows this draft, which has one key
difference from RFC 7539 (the draft uses an 8 byte nonce and 8 byte
counter while RFC 7539 uses a 12 byte nonce and 4 byte counter)
https://tools.ietf.org/html/draft-josefsson-ssh-chacha20-poly1305-openssh-00

notes.body:
avoid a warning about use of an uninitialized variable that was mentioned in https://code.wireshark.org/review/c/37997/6..7
```suggestion:-0+0
    ssh_kex_key *secret = NULL, *priv;
```

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/10/diffs?diff_id=108035982&start_sha=3d4ad90ab63ea92f9b8bf143e5778243c258296b#1bf6e4005e105405db89acc9c1073c2f14004190_1662_1662)

shouldn't this be:
```suggestion:-0+0
        secret == NULL) {
```

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/10/diffs?diff_id=108035982&start_sha=3d4ad90ab63ea92f9b8bf143e5778243c258296b#1bf6e4005e105405db89acc9c1073c2f14004190_1747_1747)

Can you be sure that `key->data` is at least/exactly 64 bytes in all cases? It is supposed to be like that, but is a malicious capture/configuration able to trigger other conditions? If so, please add a defence-in-depth or assertion check to catch that.

Let me think. I don't think so, but I assume you have looked into it and are right.

In this specific patch, in ssh_derive_symmetric_key, need = 64 (for this cipher, it's set based on the cipher in a later patch IIRC), and the key->data will be generated until it is >= 64. I can't see how anyone could provide data which is turned into <= 64. But in that case, perhaps an assert is in order since it should never happen?
It might be true now, but not when the code is changed in the future. Adding an assertion if it cannot happen sounds good to me.

Running with ASAN and memory leak detection enabled (`export ASAN_OPTIONS=fast_unwind_on_malloc=0` for more accurate traces) revealed some resource leaks:
```
    #5 0x7f116b62fcb2 in gcry_cipher_open (/usr/lib/libgcrypt.so.20+0xccb2)
    #6 0x7f117cb407c6 in ssh_decryption_setup_cipher epan/dissectors/packet-ssh.c:1896:13
    #7 0x7f117cb3f1fd in ssh_derive_symmetric_keys epan/dissectors/packet-ssh.c:1808:5
    #8 0x7f117cb3df41 in ssh_keylog_compute_hash epan/dissectors/packet-ssh.c:1763:5
    #9 0x7f117cb3a730 in ssh_dissect_key_exchange epan/dissectors/packet-ssh.c:983:21
    #10 0x7f117cb31663 in ssh_dissect_ssh2 epan/dissectors/packet-ssh.c:630:18
    #11 0x7f117cb2da37 in dissect_ssh epan/dissectors/packet-ssh.c:569:26
```

Have a look at `wmem_register_callback` as used in `wg_prepare_handshake_keys` (packet-wireguard.c). This callback can be set after the structure is created:
```
        global_data = (struct ssh_flow_data *)wmem_alloc0(wmem_file_scope(), sizeof(struct ssh_flow_data));
```

I can't reproduce that memory leak actually. I set the environment variable, and built with -DENABLE_ASAN=1. I'll try to rebuild it with that setting again, maybe something changed since last time.

Alright I hadn't exported another variable. I'm checking.
